newsitem.title: EGYPT: Cairo bourse slips in slumbering in holiday mood.
newsitem.headline: Cairo bourse slips in slumbering in holiday mood.

text.p: Egypt's languid stock market slumped on Tuesday in half-hearted trading made sluggish by a steady stream of long weekends.

The Capital Market Authority overall index slipped 3.34 points to 385.67 on its first day of trading since Thursday. The market was closed for a four-day weekend to celebrate Coptic Easter and will shut again on Thursday for Labour Day.
"The market is slow, lazy and boring," said broker Sherif Cararah of brokers Hermes-EFG. "There's not much local attention because of the holidays."
But Cararah said the slow trading was a "golden chance" for investors whom he said would not see such low prices again for at least one month.

"There's lots of supply now which will dry up. We expect the market to pick by my mid-May or June and we'll see sharp rises fuelled by local and foreign interest. It will be a different market by the summer," he said.
Brokers have said that foreign investors have bombarded them with queries about the market and they expect the information gathering would be transformed to action by May.
Cararah said that institutions were behind almost all of Tuesday's trading, worth a below-average 48.7 million pounds ($14.35 million).
The perennial cement and milling firms topped turnover, which also saw trading in a smattering of pharmaceutical, housing and fertiliser companies.

Brokers said the state's announcement on Friday that it would privatise up to 4.2 million shares in Suez Cement with a market value of about 300 million pounds ($89 million) added more shine to the popular sector.

Four companies -- Helwan Portland Cement, Amriyah Portland Cement, Egyptian Portland Tora Cement and Alexandria Portland Cement -- own the 4.2 million shares which are about 8.5 percent of Suez's equity.
"The sale will boost the firms' results and because they have different sizes, but equal stakes in Suez, the privatisation will affect them differently," Cararah said.
Helwan was the most active stock, rising 0.51 pounds to 79.51 in trade worth 5.52 million. Amriyah came second with 3.7 million of trading but shares ended lower 0.9 pounds at 88.5.

Alexandria Portland Cement did well, rising 2.85 pounds to 72.1. Cararah said that Alexandria had the most to gain from selling its stake in Suez because it was the smallest company in terms of capital and production.

Milling firms were mixed but brokers said North Cairo Flour Mills fixed investor attention after an announcement that it would retain its market share and revamp some of its mills. The shares closed 0.25 pounds higher at 191.25.
Heliopolis Housing and Development also rose 1.00 to 431.00 and fertiliser firm Egyptian Financial and Industrial gained 2.75 to 220.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 576.62 points from 590.58 on Thursday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 272.16 from 272.09
